messages:
alex: CI red on canary image publish. Kaniko finalize step failed with 401 + unexpected EOF right after I moved a chown into a different RUN. Anyone seen this pattern?

ci-bot: Buildkite #1423 — image-publish: FAILED. kaniko: error when uploading layer: unexpected EOF; registry returned 401 when finalizing upload. Logs: ```error: unexpected EOF
http 401 unauthorized
layer 7 checksum mismatch?```

jamie: Re-run first. 401+EOF can be token hiccup, but checksum/EOF also smells like cache/chunk corruption after layer reorder.

alex: Kicked a manual rerun (https://buildkite.example/1423).

mike: If rerun still fails, try --no-cache or flip chown to be earlier/later to avoid changing layer boundaries. Did the Dockerfile change add a large COPY + chown in the same RUN?

sarah: We rotated staging registry creds overnight, but infra said rollouts complete. @infra: any rate-limiting or proxy errors from the registry?

jamie: Quick grep of kaniko logs shows checksum mismatch for layer 7 right before auth error. Workaround: run kaniko with `--no-cache` or `--force` to avoid pulling cached layer blobs. Also consider buildx --pull.

alex: Rerun failed again with same 401. Starting a kaniko run with `--no-cache` now.

ci-bot: manual job #1424 started (kaniko --no-cache).

mike: :thumbsup: If no-cache succeeds, we should avoid big chown moves in one RUN. Layer boundary changes cause subtle upload/validation issues.

sarah: If no-cache works, please open a bisect issue so we can find the exact Dockerfile change that triggered corrupted cache uploads.

alex: No-cache succeeded and image pushed. Creating a follow-up PR to split the chown and add a note in devdocs about layer-safe Dockerfile edits. Opening issue #5123 for bisect + docs + retry-on-push fallback.

jamie: :rocket: nice. I'll add a small infra task to detect big layer boundary changes during CI and suggest `--no-cache` when push fails with checksum/EOF errors.
